issues.legal_issue: A payment described as earnest money or a deposit attracts a buyer’s statutory charge for repayment and interest when, in substance, it was prepaid purchase money and the seller’s failure to complete the sale makes it refundable.
material_facts: The buyers paid a sum on execution of an agreement for sale, with other payments contemplated at later stages.
The agreement described the payment as a deposit or earnest money and provided for its return with interest if the sellers failed to perform specified obligations.
The structure and terms of the agreement showed that the payment was intended both as security and as part payment of the purchase price.
The sale was not completed because of the sellers’ lapses and inability to perform, and the buyers had not improperly declined delivery.
issues.conclusion: The payment was, prima facie, prepaid purchase money, so the statutory charge covered its repayment and the interest due under the agreement.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 55(6)(b) of the Transfer of Property Act, a buyer has a charge on the seller’s interest in the property for purchase money properly paid in anticipation of delivery and interest on that amount; the charge also extends to earnest money in the circumstances specified in the section. Whether a sum is earnest money, a deposit, or an advance depends on the parties’ intention and the surrounding circumstances, not merely the label used. Earnest money may serve both as part payment and as security. The court relied on (Kunwar) Chiranjit Singh v. Har Swarup, AIR 1926 PC 1, and Maula Bux v. Union of India, AIR 1970 SC 1955, and described the charge as grounded in justice, equity and good conscience.

rule.if: buyer_seeks_refund_after_failed_property_sale_contract and payment_was_part_of_purchase_price and seller_failed_to_complete_sale and buyer_did_not_improperly_refuse_delivery

predicates.buyer_seeks_refund_after_failed_property: A buyer seeks repayment of money paid under a contract for the sale of property after the sale fails.
predicates.payment_was_part_of_purchase_price: The payment, considered in light of the agreement and surrounding circumstances, formed part of the purchase price rather than being only security for performance.
predicates.seller_failed_to_complete_sale: The seller’s failure or inability to perform prevented completion of the sale.
predicates.buyer_did_not_improperly_refuse_delivery: The buyer did not improperly refuse to accept delivery of the property.

issues.definition: When a buyer seeks repayment after a failed property sale contract, the payment was part of the purchase price, the seller failed to complete the sale, and the buyer did not improperly refuse delivery, the buyer has a property charge for repayment and interest.

issues.legal_issue: A temporary injunction against dealing with property may be maintained to protect a buyer’s statutory charge securing repayment and interest while the buyer’s claim is pending.
material_facts: The buyers sued for repayment and interest and sought an injunction against sale, alienation, encumbrance, or other dealings with the property pending trial.
The sellers had returned the principal payment but disputed liability for interest.
The High Court’s Single Judge granted the temporary injunction on the basis that the buyer’s charge covered the unpaid interest.
The Supreme Court held that the payment was prima facie prepaid purchase money and that the statutory charge covered repayment and interest.
issues.conclusion: The Single Judge’s order granting the temporary injunction was restored and was to remain in force pending disposal of the suit.
issues.legal_principle: Section 55(6)(b) of the Transfer of Property Act gives the buyer a statutory charge on the seller’s interest in the property for qualifying purchase money and interest. Where that charge secures the buyer’s pending claim, the property may be protected by a temporary injunction. The Court rejected the Division Bench’s view that the charge could not secure interest on the payment in the circumstances of this case.

predicates.appeal_concerns_interim_property_injunct: An appeal concerns an interim order sought to prevent dealings with property while a suit is pending.
predicates.buyer_has_prima_facie_property_charge: The buyer has a prima facie property charge securing the claim against the seller.
predicates.buyer_claim_remains_pending: The buyer’s claim secured by the charge remains to be decided in the pending suit.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns an interim property injunction, the buyer has a prima facie property charge, and the secured claim remains pending, property dealings are restrained pending the suit.

issues.legal_issue: A court hearing a pending suit may permit a sale of property otherwise subject to an interim restraint if sufficient sale proceeds are secured to protect the buyer’s claim.
material_facts: The sellers submitted that a complete freeze on sale could prevent development of the property and asked to be allowed to sell with the trial court’s permission and safeguards.
The Supreme Court left the parties at liberty to apply to the court hearing the suit for permission to sell.

The Court directed that the court hearing the suit could consider permission after hearing the buyers and requiring enough of the sale consideration to be deposited in court to protect their claims pending the suit’s outcome.
issues.conclusion: The parties may seek permission from the court hearing the suit to sell the property, and that court may permit the sale if sufficient sale proceeds are deposited to safeguard the buyers’ claims.
issues.legal_principle: The Court preserved the interim protection of the buyer’s claim while allowing the court hearing the suit to consider a request to sell. Any permission is subject to hearing the buyer and securing in court the portion of the sale consideration necessary to meet the buyer’s claim pending the final decision.

predicates.property_sale_is_restrained_pending_suit: An interim order restrains the seller from dealing with the property while the suit is pending.
predicates.seller_seeks_permission_to_sell: The seller asks the court hearing the suit for permission to sell the property.
predicates.sale_proceeds_can_be_secured_for_buyer_c: Sufficient sale proceeds can be deposited or otherwise secured to protect the buyer’s claim pending the suit.

issues.definition: When a sale is restrained pending suit, the seller seeks permission to sell, and sufficient proceeds can be secured for the buyer’s claim, the court may allow the sale subject to security.
